h: פָּרָשַׁת שְׁקָלִים, מַאֲמָר י״ג Parshas Shekalim — Maamar Yud Gimmel

p: so that the shekalim would be brought to the Mikdash,
when we have no Mikdash and no mizbeach,
that it is so that the saying be reckoned like the deed,
as with the verses of the korbanos,
for the essence of the mitzvah of shekalim
is that korbanos be bought with them,
and what use are the shekalim
דִּכְתִיב [שְׁמוֹת ל, טו] לָתֵת אֶת תְּרוּמַת ה׳
it is written (Shemos 30:15), "to give the offering of Hashem
and in its plain sense, what atonement
has no involvement at all in korbanos
he has already completed the deed on his part
וְכֵן קָרוּ לֵיהּ כֶּסֶף הַכִּפּוּרִים [שָׁם, טז]
And so it is called "the atonement money" (ibid. 16)
the Yisrael completed the atonement on his part.
And this is what we say in the piyut (Mussaf, at the blessing of Modim):
"May the pure utterance of our lips
meaning that through reading the parsha
it will be as if one gave his shekel,
and the atonement will be completed
as in the time of the Beis HaMikdash
when they would give the shekalim,
and it will serve to atone.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Tzav 6 — “The completion of the deed is also from Hashem, as it says ‘in your mouth and in your heart to do it,’ and not ‘in your deeds.’” Rav Tzadok there generalizes the principle at work here: a Jew’s share in any mitzvah is what lies in his power, and once he has done that, the deed is reckoned complete even though others, or Hashem, carry it out.

paragraphs.text: Exodus 30:15–16 — “The wealthy shall not give more, and the poor shall not give less, than half a shekel, when giving the Lord’s contribution to atone for your lives. You shall take the atonement money from the children of Israel and assign it to the service of the Tent of Meeting; it shall be a memorial before the Lord for the children of Israel, to atone for your lives.” Both the act of giving and the money itself carry the language of atonement. Rav Tzadok distinguishes the donor’s completed part from the later purchase and offering of sacrifices.

paragraphs.text: Mussaf piyyut for Parshas Shekalim, Modim — “The One who counts counted them in the five books, and another five in all the books. May the pure utterance of our lips make payment for bulls, for the silver of atonement shekels has ceased. May the light of Your face shine upon us, O Master; I shall bear the shekel in the established and exalted House.” The source directly connects the lips’ utterance with payment for sacrificial bulls when the shekel contribution is unavailable. Rav Tzadok explains reading the Torah portion as completing Israel’s part in atonement.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Maharal, Gevuros Hashem 69 — on “I have already instituted for them the order of offerings; when they read it I count it as if they offered them”: “The offering is the return of the effect to its cause in deed, and the Torah of the offerings is the order of that return.” Maharal explains why reading can atone as the act did, the premise of Rav Tzadok’s claim that reading Parshas Shekalim completes atonement as in Temple times.
